evidence.field: 校 entry; graphic analysis and earliest dictionary gloss
evidence.text: The entry reads 校（ ）: 木囚也。從木交聲 — ‘a wooden restraint for a prisoner’; it analyzes 木 as the semantic element and 交 as phonetic. This is the Han-period lexicographer’s account, not independent proof of the character’s earliest physical form.
evidence.title: 說文解字/06

evidence.field: 校; explanation and cited classical uses
evidence.text: The database likewise describes 木製刑具 as the basic sense and gives the Shuowen and Duan Yucai explanation. It cites the *Zhouyi* line 履校滅趾 for a restraint, then lists extensions to a barrier (墨子; 漢書), a military unit (戰國策; 漢書), and textual checking. These attestations are presented as separate sense uses; they do not by themselves date every semantic transition.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫 — 校

evidence.source: Ministry of Education, Taiwan, Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants
evidence.field: 校; pronunciation variants and sense divisions
evidence.text: The entry distinguishes jiào (including restraint, barrier, horse-keeping and military organization, correction/checking) from xiào (place of teaching/learning and military rank). It cites 孟子·滕文公上 for 夏曰校 and 周禮·夏官·校人 for the horse-keeping organization. The *Mengzi* passage is evidence for a school-related use in the transmitted text, not proof that 校 originated graphically as ‘school’.
evidence.title: 教育部《異體字字典》— 校

evidence.source: Mengzi, Teng Wen Gong (online classical text)
evidence.field: 夏曰校 passage
evidence.text: The passage says 庠者養也，校者教也 and 夏曰校，殷曰序，周曰庠. This records an association of 校 with a teaching place in the transmitted *Mengzi* text; it does not establish when the meaning first arose or that the graph developed from the restraint sense by a specific route.
evidence.title: 滕文公 · 孟子

evidence.source: Ministry of Education, Taiwan, Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants
evidence.field: 校; sound readings and sources
evidence.text: The dictionary records Mandarin jiào and xiào, and cites historical fanqie sources including 胡敎切 and 古孝切. Those traditional readings support distinct historical reading traditions, but this entry does not reconstruct Old Chinese pronunciations.

editorial_rules: Write about the character's graphic history; distinguish it from the history of a spoken word.
Separate historical explanation from mnemonics. Do not infer history from modern shapes or readings.
Sources may repeat one another. A source count is not independent corroboration.
Treat Shuowen as a historical account, not automatic confirmation. Its generated English glosses are excluded.
Unrelated word senses may appear in Wiktionary excerpts. Do not merge them into a character origin.
Related-character evidence retains its record_character. Do not silently transfer a traditional form's components to a simplified form.
No glyph image has been visually inspected in this packet. Do not claim to have inspected one.
Explain missing evidence explicitly, especially for Japanese-created characters. A Chinese spelling pronunciation is not evidence for a Japanese origin.

gaps: No dated oracle-bone or bronze inscription for 校 was verified. The displayed CUHK entry includes small-seal and manuscript image slots, but the available page text does not provide dating or a traceable early form sequence.

The source of school-related 校 is unresolved: 孟子 records 夏曰校 and explains 校者教也, but the graphic-semantic bridge from ‘wooden restraint’ or ‘barrier’ to ‘school’ is not established by the sources inspected. Treat a proposed barrier-to-enclosure-to-school link as an inference, not a demonstrated chronology.

Semantic chronology remains incomplete. Separate classical citations support restraint, barrier, stable/military organization, checking, and school uses, but the searched sources do not establish first dates for each sense or a secure ordered chain among them.

The dossier’s *kreːw/*kreːws notation is not identified as a reconstruction system in the excerpt. Baxter–Sagart’s inspected table gives 交 *[k]ˤraw, but omits 校; a character-specific host reconstruction and a directly comparable same-system pair were not recovered. Phonetic role is asserted by Shuowen and supported by the visible shared 交 element, but reconstruction-level historical sound matching remains unverified.

Only a local 校 Mandarin row xiào was supplied; local searches did not locate an exact 交 kMandarin row or a 校 Baxter–Sagart row. The official Unicode character-specific record URLs were tried but inaccessible, so they cannot serve as verified click-through evidence here.
No independently dated early physical inscription image was inspected. The Commons seal drawing is explicitly a Shuowen-style rendering and is not suitable evidence for ancient chronology.
A purported Baxter–Sagart discussion in an Italian dissertation appeared in search results, but the PDF returned 403; no claim from that inaccessible page is relied upon.
No dated oracle-bone, bronze, or other independently dated early inscription for 校 was verified. The Commons candidate is a modern redraw of a Shuowen seal form, not an artifact image.

The phonetic role 交 is asserted by Shuowen and the Ministry dictionary. This research did not establish an independently comparable same-system historical reconstruction for both 交 and 校; the local Baxter–Sagart table row provided for 交 does not include 校.

The origin and sound of any supposed physical object behind the graph are not independently established here; the Shuowen restraint gloss alone does not establish a whole-graph phonetic loan or the name of a depicted tool.

Separate citations attest several transmitted senses, but the sources inspected do not establish their earliest dates or a secure semantic chain. In particular, the school sense occurs in the transmitted Mengzi and does not establish a graphic or semantic transition from restraint, barrier, or enclosure.
